name: Title Fight
label: Revelation
lede: Two twelve-year-old twins and their friend named a band after a cable TV guide, ran shows in an abandoned pizza shop, and ended up rewiring a generation of hardcore kids toward shoegaze.

eras.title: Twelve years old in Kingston
eras.text: Ned and Ben Russin were twelve when they started Title Fight in Kingston, Pennsylvania, with Jamie Rhoden. Their older brother Alex Russin of Cold World had handed them punk records and a way into the hardcore circuit, and the kids ran with it, all the way into an abandoned pizza shop.

years.h: Title Fight named after an HBO/Showtime guide cover
years.p: Twins Ned (bass) and Ben Russin (drums), twelve years old, start Title Fight in Kingston, Pennsylvania, with Jamie Rhoden on guitar. Ned finds the name on an old HBO/Showtime guide in the attic.
years.xp:
Their brother Alex Russin had given the twins [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] and [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] records around 1997. When Alex left for college, they raided the CDs he left behind and started learning instruments with a band in mind.

The first demo, Down for the Count, came out the same year, self-released.

years.h: Title Fight's first show: Frost Bite's last one
years.p: Title Fight open the final show by Alex Russin's band Frost Bite, on a bill with [[Blacklisted|00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6]], Drug Test and Scraps and Heartattacks.
years.xp: An early booking came from promoter Bobb Mac, who said yes to the kids on one condition: because of their brother Alex, they had to cover [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]]. Eight years later Gorilla Biscuits' [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] produced their first album.

years.h: High-schoolers open The Future in an abandoned pizza shop
years.p: Title Fight build a stage in an empty pizza restaurant and run an illegal squat venue called The Future, hosting [[Coalesce|3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2]], Mental, Renee Heartfelt and More to Pride before it shuts.

years.h: Shane Moran joins Title Fight on second guitar
years.p: Shane Moran becomes Title Fight's second guitarist, and the band starts drawing real attention in a Kingston, Scranton and Doylestown scene that includes [[Tigers Jaw|3cdf1327-39eb-4ffe-9ce3-20599ac6a468]] and [[Balance and Composure|0d20c42d-133c-429d-8f76-3c2458aee3e8]].

years.h: A Fireworks tour puts Title Fight in front of Run for Cover
years.p: On a summer tour with [[Fireworks|7a7b70f3-1d6f-40f1-8c55-f75a376bee87]] and [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]], Title Fight catch the ear of Jeff Casazza, owner of Boston's Run for Cover Records. They also split a record with The Erection Kids on Flight Plan.

eras.title: Dropping out to get in the van
eras.text: The Kingston 7" pointed Title Fight toward emo and melodic hardcore, and Run for Cover gave them a label. After The Last Thing You Forget all four members left school to tour full time, and their hometown lost its all-ages room.

years.h: Kingston 7" on Flight Plan Records
years.p: Title Fight's hometown 7" is the turn from pop-punk toward emo and melodic hardcore. Fifteen years later the band starts its own label, Purple Circle, just to press Kingston again.

years.h: Title Fight sign to Run for Cover Records
years.p: Run for Cover signs Title Fight, and in December they record with producer [[Jay Maas|8784da50-4dd3-4b54-8b01-948157c56f20]] at the Getaway Group in Massachusetts.

years.h: The Last Thing You Forget · Run for Cover
years.p: Three new Jay Maas-produced songs, with the CD gathering everything the band had released before. Artwork by John Slaby from Wilkes-Barre.
years.xp:
After it came out, all four members dropped out of school to tour full time, with [[Crime in Stereo|2bad20e7-61c8-4aa1-afcc-ca6f060ccb71]], Fireworks, [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]], [[Bayside|5f821136-9935-403c-abb5-e78ddda35e9f]], [[Senses Fail|b4946461-dacb-4aa9-a77c-7b3231317794]], Balance and Composure and [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]].

Shane Moran and Jamie Rhoden also ran a hardcore side band, Bad Seed, whose 2009 EP came out on 6131 Records, while Moran and the Russins played in the straight edge band [[Disengage|cc0877e2-6c3c-4af6-904f-d5c1c6fc1fc4]].

years.h: Cafe Metropolis, where Title Fight played first, closes
years.p: Cafe Metropolis, the room where Title Fight played their first show, shuts, leaving Title Fight's scene without a home. The band's song Dreamcatchers lands on Triple B Records' America's Hardcore comp the same year.

eras.title: Shed, a DIY room, and Floral Green
eras.text: A Gorilla Biscuits founder produced the debut album, the band opened its own all-ages space modeled on 924 Gilman, and then Floral Green turned the hardcore kids on to Dinosaur Jr. and Sonic Youth. It reached the Billboard 200.

years.h: Title Fight sign to SideOneDummy Records
years.p: SideOneDummy signs Title Fight for their first full-length. The free single 27 follows on February 10.

years.h: Title Fight open the Redwood Art Space
years.p: Title Fight and local friends open the Redwood Art Space, an all-ages, alcohol-free venue modeled on Berkeley's 924 Gilman Street. Landlord and government pressure force it to move in June 2012.

years.h: Shed, produced by Walter Schreifels
years.p: [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] of Gorilla Biscuits and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] produces Title Fight's debut album, with [[Will Yip|282e2957-fd09-4260-babf-50f1d57eeb75]] engineering, and sings on Safe in Your Skin. It debuts at No. 8 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

years.h: Title Fight play Reading and Leeds
years.p: After a first headline tour with [[The Menzingers|3071d829-b9ca-4499-b4f5-74d6d8531aed]] and [[Touché Amoré|ea367e3c-4c74-460b-8a99-bbbb9b1ad5cf]] and a July run through the UK and Europe, Title Fight play England's Reading and Leeds festivals.

years.h: Title Fight tour Japan, then support Rise Against
years.p: Title Fight play Japan's Alliance Trax A.T. Tour in February, then open for [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]] across the US in April and May.

years.h: Floral Green hits No. 69 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Produced by Will Yip, Floral Green swaps pop-punk for fuzz, with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]], [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in its DNA. NPR premiered Sympathy in August.
years.xp:
BrooklynVegan's Andrew Sacher later called it one of the most pivotal albums of its generation, for hardcore and for guitar-based rock and punk in general, and credited it with helping set up hardcore's 2020s breakthrough.

The record release show was in Warrior Run, Pennsylvania, with The Menzingers, Tigers Jaw and Gypsy. The same month Title Fight made their first trip to Australia, with Touché Amoré.

eras.title: One Revelation 7", then the blur
eras.text: Between Floral Green and Hyperview, Title Fight stopped at Revelation for four songs, the label that had put out the Gorilla Biscuits records they'd been made to cover as kids. Then they signed to ANTI- and made a shoegaze album.

years.h: Title Fight split a 7" with Touché Amoré
years.p: Title Fight and Touché Amoré, tour partners in the US and Australia, share a split 7".

years.h: Spring Songs EP · Revelation REV 154
years.p: Four songs in just over twelve minutes, produced by Will Yip. Revelation's first pressing runs 1,512 on clear orange and 2,650 on opaque orange vinyl.
years.xp:
SPIN premiered Be a Toy in August. Its video, directed by Susy Cereijo, was shot on Super 8 during the band's spring European tour.

Revelation said the deal gave Title Fight room to move, and the band used it: Pitchfork gave the EP 7.2, while Vice didn't like it.

years.h: Title Fight play Coachella
years.p: The kids from the Kingston pizza-shop squat play Coachella in 2014, the photo that later heads Title Fight's Wikipedia page.

years.h: Title Fight sign to ANTI- and record Hyperview
years.p: Title Fight announce a deal with ANTI- and spend July and August at Studio 4 in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania, making Hyperview with Will Yip.

years.h: Actor Mark Burnham stars in Title Fight's Chlorine video
years.p: The Fader premieres the video for Chlorine, directed by Johnny Look and starring character actor Mark Burnham. Pitchfork hears No Age and DIIV in its flanged guitars, not Warped Tour.

years.h: Hyperview, Title Fight's last album · ANTI-
years.p: Shoegaze and dream pop, with Ned Russin citing [[The Beach Boys|ebfc1398-8d96-47e3-82c3-f782abcdb13d]]' Pet Sounds. It reaches No. 78 on the Billboard 200; the release show is at the Gallery of Sound record store in Wilkes-Barre.
years.xp:
Ned Russin called it the most melodic, simple stuff they'd ever written. Some critics resisted the change; Metacritic landed at 71.

The tours that year paired them with Merchandise and [[Power Trip|7f179acc-d6eb-4ca9-af90-c14e397fb613]] in the US, and with Milk Teeth, Cold World and [[Drug Church|32d2897c-4c91-46db-8161-f51d3f4f0d93]] in Europe.

eras.title: Never said goodbye
eras.text: Title Fight didn't announce a breakup. They just played less, then a festival in England, then a benefit on Long Island, and then nothing, while each of them started something else.

years.h: Unreleased Dust Collector goes to an Orlando benefit
years.p: After the Pulse nightclub shooting, Title Fight give the Hyperview outtake Dust Collector to Forever Beautiful, a Bandcamp comp for the OneOrlando Fund with Turnstile, Citizen and Modern Baseball.

years.big: "If this is it, it's been a wild and beautiful ride."
q: If this is it, it's been a wild and beautiful ride.
years.h: Ned Russin's goodbye-that-isn't at Outbreak Festival
years.p: Headlining England's Outbreak Festival, their second-to-last show, Ned Russin tells the crowd this might be it. The same year he starts his solo project [[Glitterer|fb29a165-203d-497b-9a01-fc48f4dba65c]].

years.h: Title Fight's last show: a Long Island benefit with Turnstile
years.p: Title Fight play Revolution Bar & Music Hall in Amityville, New York, for their longtime friend and tour mate Aaron Warman and his family. [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]] open. It's their last show.

eras.title: A B-side takes over TikTok
eras.text: With the band silent, a Shed deep cut became their biggest song, the hardcore boom they'd helped set up arrived, and the drummer joined Citizen. Ned Russin kept saying the same thing: nobody ever said it was over.

years.big: 118 million plays for a song that was never a single
q: Title Fight was the first one that really affected everybody.
years.h: Safe in Your Skin goes viral, eleven years late
years.p: Safe in Your Skin, the Shed track Walter Schreifels sings on, takes off on TikTok in 2022 and 2023. By November 2025 it's Title Fight's most-streamed Spotify song, at 118 million plays.
years.xp: Citizen's Mat Kerekes put Title Fight's reach bluntly: every band in their world was influenced by Title Fight, even if they didn't know it. Wikipedia's list of bands citing them runs from Turnover and The Story So Far to Ethel Cain.

years.h: Ben Russin becomes Citizen's drummer
years.p: Ben Russin joins [[Citizen|bd743cdc-74a1-4669-bcf9-3942594dc09a]] and plays on their album Calling the Dogs. In September, members of Title Fight start the Purple Circle label to re-press Kingston.

years.h: Title Fight reunite, acoustic, at Ben Russin's wedding
years.p: Ned Russin, Jamie Rhoden and Shane Moran play together for the first time since 2018, at drummer Ben Russin's wedding, covering Walter Schreifels's Requiem. Alex Russin joins Rhoden on [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]]'s Slide Away.
years.xp:
Stereogum compared it to stories of Fugazi quietly practicing in D.C. basements: a reunion for themselves and nobody else.

Ned Russin's line on the band's status hasn't changed: they never said hiatus, never said broken up, and any band might play again.
